notes: ACCESS: Tier 1 direct HTTP (curl) and headless Playwright/Chromium both returned HTTP 429 'Access to this page has been denied' (PerimeterX px-captcha) on every URL, including the homepage and category pages. robots.txt carries no Claude-specific disallow and no site-wide Disallow:/, so proceeded down the access-tier ladder: curl_cffi TLS-impersonation (still HTTP-tier, no rendering) with profile chrome124 passed cleanly (HTTP 200, full 1.1MB+ page) on every category URL tried; safari17_0/safari18_0/safari184_ios/chrome131/chrome120 also worked, chrome110/edge101/safari18_0_ios/plain-curl did not. Playwright with real Chrome channel hung/timed out in this sandbox and was abandoned once curl_cffi proved reliable and complete (full SSR HTML with H1, breadcrumb, item-count and a first-page product sample) -- did not need Claude-in-Chrome. DISCOVERY: robots.txt's seo-category-index.xml -> seo-category-sitemap~0.xml gave the site's curated 513-URL top category tree (unprotected, per prior project learning that Wayfair sitemaps bypass PerimeterX). Grepped it for Christmas/Halloween/Diwali/Valentine/Easter/Thanksgiving/New Year/Holi/Rakhi/Eid/Hanukkah/festive/seasonal/mother's-father's-day/St Patrick's etc. Cross-checked against the full category-link list embedded in the 'Holiday Decor' hub page itself (which surfaced 2 nodes -- Father's Day, Valentine's Day -- missing from the curated sitemap). Confirmed via breadcrumb JSON that all Seasonal categories nest either under /christmas-decorations/ (own branch) or /holiday-decor/ (mothers-day, fathers-day, new-years-eve, halloween-decorations, easter-decorations, valentines-day, seasonal-decor > {spring,summer,autumn,winter}-decor). No Diwali, Eid, Hanukkah, Thanksgiving, Holi, Rakhi, or St Patrick's category exists anywhere in the 513-URL sitemap or the Holiday Decor hub's ~191 linked categories -- UK storefront does not carry these, consistent with the task brief's expectation that the UK mix differs from the US site (se1.json, 13 holiday nodes). CONTENT VERIFICATION / EXCLUSIONS: 5 candidate nodes were investigated and excluded as non-genuine broad/generic merchandising buckets rather than real curated seasonal categories, despite carrying real ProductCategory IDs and holiday-sounding names: 'New Year's Eve', 'Seasonal Decor', 'Spring Decor' all display a literal capped 'Over 50,000 Items' (Wayfair's own uncounted-overflow label, not an exact count); 'Winter Decor' (18,684) and 'Summer Decor' (20,554) carry implausibly large non-capped counts of the same order of magnitude as the entire Christmas branch. Product samples for all five, taken across 4-6 independent re-fetches each (to rule out a one-off unlucky sample), were consistently 100% generic wall-art/cushion/mattress/storage-shed items with zero winter/summer/spring/new-year-specific naming -- these read as un-curated 'browse everything' pages that happen to sit in the seasonal nav branch, not genuine seasonal PLPs (rules SS4/SS6). Excluded per SS4/SS17: christmas-sale, christmas-tableware-linens-sale, christmas-home-accents-sale, christmas-trees-tree-decor-sale, christmas-wreaths-garland-sale, christmas-textiles-sale, holiday-decor-sale (all pure promotional variants of an included category). The 'Holiday Decor' root hub (c1863206) was not recorded as a row -- it is the site's internal taxonomy container name, not itself a holiday, and its own item count was unstable across identical re-fetches (18,684 then 15,761), further confirming it is not a discrete counted category. MANUAL-REVIEW FLAGS: Father's Day (50 items, framed 'Father's Day Gift Ideas') and Easter Decorations (317 items, framed 'Easter Decorations Selection') both have genuine distinct categoryIds, non-capped realistic counts, and explicit occasion framing, but their sampled first-page products (mugs/wall-art-prints for Father's Day; table runners/placemats/napkins for Easter) carried no explicit Dad/Father's-Day or Easter-egg/bunny branding across repeated fetches -- included because Mother's Day (same tier, same page shape) DID surface explicitly branded items (Mother's Day apron, Mother's Day card) validating that this tier of the taxonomy is a real curated 'gift ideas' layer, but flagged for a human to double check given the weaker per-row evidence. Autumn Decor (349) included with lighter confidence -- unlike its Winter/Summer/Spring/Seasonal siblings, its sample surfaced explicitly autumn-themed items (wreath with pumpkins, faux autumn swag) alongside generic ones. HIERARCHY NOTE: 'Christmas Decorations' (the branch root, 18,342 items) is recorded as a grouping row since its 10 captured children below are a near-complete enumeration of the branch per the sitemap. 'Christmas Home Accents' (10,230) and 'Christmas Trees & Decorations' (5,909) are themselves parents of further sub-links visible on their pages (e.g. Christmas Wall Art, Christmas Candles, Christmas Advent Calendars, Christmas Stockings under Home Accents; Christmas Tree Toppers, Baubles & Ornaments under Trees) that do not have their own URLs in the 513-URL sitemap and so were not separately enumerated -- these two are kept as their own valid rows (real qty+evidence) rather than nulled to a grouping row, to avoid discarding real site-reported data for an incompletely-captured child set. 'Christmas Tableware & Linens' (360) is kept as its own row alongside its 3 captured children (Dinnerware & Drinkware 264, Serveware 283, Kitchen Linens 377) even though the children's counts sum to more than the parent's -- proof these are independently-computed overlapping facet counts, not a strict subset sum, so none were nulled out. 'Outdoor Christmas Decorations' (753) is kept as its own row alongside its parent 'Christmas Home Accents' per the Seasonal category's explicit overlap-tolerant rule. ADJUDICATION (2026-09-04): removed the 'Father's Day' row (50 items, https://www.wayfair.co.uk/holiday-decor/cat/fathers-day-c1867757.html) - sampled products across 6 independent re-fetches (Ceramic Coffee Mug, wall-art canvas prints) carried no dad/father-specific branding, and the page's 'Gift Ideas You'll Love' framing is a generic templated title reused across the sibling Easter/Mother's Day nodes rather than occasion-specific content, matching the generic-catalog-mislabeled-as-holiday pattern.
